findings.title: Error-query check is a substring match and false-positives on exclusions
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` lowercases `request.GET['query']` and returns true if it contains the substring `event.type:error`. That matches queries that are not error-focused, including the common discover filters `!event.type:error` and `NOT event.type:error`, as well as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. For an allowlisted project on the discover dataset, those queries rewrite `count()` to `sum(sample_weight)`. Transaction rows often have no error sample weight (or a different transaction sampling weight), so the events-stats request either 500s in Snuba or returns wildly inflated transaction counts. The same check misses real error queries such as `event.type:[error]`. Nothing in the new tests covers a negated or list-form `event.type` filter.

findings.title: Upsampled count sums sample_weight, which this change never writes
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no null fallback, and the column rewrite assumes every event in an allowlisted project has a meaningful sample_weight. Nothing in this PR sets that column. The only new writer is the test helper `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling`, which stores `sample_rate` equal to `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` (0.1 in the snuba test) and never sets `sample_weight` to `1/rate`. ClickHouse `sum` skips nulls and `toInt64` of an all-null sum is 0, so events without a weight disappear instead of counting as 1. The new stats test expects each single stored event to become `count == 10`; that cannot happen unless an unshown pipeline converts sample_rate 0.1 into sample_weight 10. Allowlisted project charts will undercount or show zeros, including for historical events ingested before weights existed.

findings.title: Top-events ranking still uses raw count() while the series is upsampled
findings.body: When upsampling is on, only `timeseries_columns` / `y_axes` are rewritten to `upsampled_count()`. `top_events_timeseries` still receives `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` and `selected_columns=self.get_field_list(...)` unchanged, and the RPC top-events path at the `orderby=` call just above does the same. Top-N selection therefore ranks groups by stored rows, not by `sum(sample_weight)`. With uneven client sample rates that ranking is wrong: a group with 100 real errors at 1% (1 stored row, weight 100) loses to a group with 10 unsampled errors (10 stored rows). The plotted series for the chosen groups is then upsampled, so the chart both picks the wrong groups and does not match the totals used to pick them. `equations` are also left as raw `count()`, so equation widgets diverge from the rewritten count axis.

findings.title: Accidental gitlink added without a submodule config
findings.body: This PR adds a gitlink `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a (the PR base) and does not update `.gitmodules` or any other file. That is not part of error upsampling. Merging it records a broken submodule: clones and CI checkouts have no URL for that gitlink, so the tree is dirty or the path fails to populate.

findings.title: Allowlist cache key uses process-randomized hash() and can serve the wrong decision
findings.body: Eligibility is cached for 60s under `error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}`. CPython `hash()` is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the key is not stable across gunicorn workers or between the getter and `invalidate_upsampling_cache`. Shared cache entries never hit across processes, and a delete on one worker cannot evict keys written by another; nothing in this PR calls the invalidator anyway. Within a process, a hash collision between two project-id sets stores one allowlist boolean for both, so a non-allowlisted query can be rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` (Snuba error or wrong counts) or an allowlisted query can skip upsampling. The key also omits the allowlist contents, so a cached True survives option changes for 60s. The new snuba tests mock `options.get` to different allowlists for the same projects and never clear this cache, so a locmem/Redis hit makes `test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist` and `test_error_upsampling_with_no_allowlisted_projects` assert raw counts while the helper still upsamples. `options.get` is already in-process; this extra `cache.get`/`cache.set` on every events-stats request, including spans and logs, is a hot-path regression and ties the endpoint to cache availability.

findings.title: Errors dataset always rewrites count() but upsampled_count is only registered on discover
findings.body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns true for the `sentry.snuba.errors` dataset with no query check, and the events-stats endpoint then asks that dataset to execute `upsampled_count() as count`. The new aggregate is added only inside `discover.py`'s `function_converter`. The errors dataset is a separate snuba module with its own query builder/dataset config; unless that config inherits this exact converter, `dataset=errors` requests on allowlisted projects fail field resolution or Snuba with an unknown function. The new tests never pass `dataset=errors` (they use the default dataset and one discover transaction query), so this path is untested.

findings.title: Upsampling decision ignores the dataset and query actually executed
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` and `query`, but eligibility calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(..., dataset, request)`, using the closed-over request dataset and `request.GET['query']`. `get_event_stats_factory` then calls this helper with a different dataset and a rewritten query: the dashboard split path runs discover with `({query}) AND !event.type:transaction`, and sometimes `event.type:transaction`, while the outer dataset is metrics performance. Those internal queries are therefore classified from the wrong inputs. Error-only split queries on allowlisted projects are not upsampled, and any path where the outer request looks error-focused will also rewrite a later transaction-only execution in the same request. The comment that the cached decision keeps behavior consistent across query execution is the opposite of what this does.

findings.title: Helper tests override setUp without calling super and will not run
findings.body: `ErrorUpsamplingTest.setUp` does not call `super().setUp()`. Sentry's TestCase setUp is what creates `self.user`, `self.team`, and the rest of the factory state that `self.create_project` uses (`teams=[self.team]` when teams are omitted). This setUp will raise AttributeError before any assertion, so the new unit tests do not actually cover allowlist checks, column rewrite, or the event.type filter.

findings.title: Transaction upsampling test does not wait for the event to be stored
findings.body: `test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events` calls `store_event` for a transaction and immediately queries events-stats, asserting the first bucket `count == 1`. setUp in the same class waits with `wait_for_event_count` after its error inserts, which is required because Snuba ingestion is not synchronous. Without that wait, the transaction is often invisible and the bucket is 0, so the test flakes and does not prove that transaction queries skip upsampling.
